parts.t: RECIPE 21 — Promo videos made with code: Hyperframes and Remotion
From: How to Use Claude AI to Make FREE Videos (Hyperframes) · 3 Jul 2026 · 1:02:47 livestream · watch
From: Claude Code Just Changed Content Creation Forever! (PART 2) · 30 Mar 2026 · 27:32 · watch
Both tools let Claude write a video as code, then record it to an MP4 on your own computer. No credits, only plan tokens. They are good at moving text, charts and screenshots.
They are also good at drawing a product that does not exist, which is the part you must never use.
THE ONE THING — the video frames the real pages, it never redraws them
Her promise is simple. You describe a video, Claude codes it, and a free tool records it.
"it's actually coding a website like using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript and then it's like animating that website and recording it" (5:30)
That makes it a promo tool, not an art tool. For you it splits in two:
The rule for every video: each product page shown is a PNG rendered from the real PDF, placed in the folder as a media file. The code may move it, crop it and frame it. It may not draw it.
Why this matters to you
On 12 Sep you had 46 live listings, zero sales, and a #2 rank on Etsy AU for "dementia caregiver binder". People can find you. What happens after they see a listing is the unproven part.
A short video that shows the actual pages is one way to show a buyer what they get. A video that shows pages you did not make is a refund waiting to happen.
Two warnings, straight from her own demos
The Remotion video builds a "simulated product demo" from her website:
"This is not my app. This is generated by Remotion and Claude by analyzing my website." (9:00)
"This is not at all on my website or even what my product looks like." (9:30)
The Hyperframes launch video did the same kind of thing:
"I was like, whoa, this looks better than my actual product." (31:30)

For software that is a style choice. For a printable, the pages are the product. So her "simulated demo" scene and her website-to-video skill are both off limits unless every page image in them is a real render.

Her testimonial demo pulled Google reviews of a plumber she found by search. She says "I have no affiliation with this person" (11:30). You have no reviews yet. Do not borrow anyone's, and do not make any up.

Her pick for a beginner
second
Her comparison is at 6:01. The Remotion install is at 2:30. Its faster route is npx skills add remotion-dev/skills (3:02).
The Remotion prompts are only on screen. She says "Take a screenshot of this and drop it into Claude code" (5:30). The captions never read them out, so this recipe does not reproduce them.
How Hyperframes goes, in her order
Install takes "five maybe 10 minutes" (4:02). If the plain version fails, a viewer tip she adopted was "Install Hyperframes opensource video editor" (57:01).
On storyboards: changes made early are "less expensive downstream to fix" (26:00). Her Remotion video gives the same advice (7:31).
For long jobs she prefers the terminal. She found Claude desktop "less stable" for long-running agents (13:01).
Her four prompts, as shapes
She reads four prompts aloud. Each ends in an MP4. Here is their shape, not their full text:
Beginner (8:32). An 8-second landscape video on one topic, with one strong animated visual metaphor. It ends "Keep it fast to render", which means no downloads or screenshots.
Faceless explainer (21:30). It uses the /faceless-explainer workflow, 30 seconds, styled like a "highbudget Netflix investigation", with a hook in the first 3 seconds.
Intermediate (31:00). It uses /website-to-video to make a 25-second launch video from a URL, capturing "the website's actual colors, typography, UI, and brand feel". See the warnings above.
Next level (42:31). It edits raw talking-head footage. It transcribes, removes false starts and filler, and trims pauses "over.3 seconds" (43:00).
Then it picks a visual per key idea, keeps one recurring motif, syncs each graphic to the moment it is spoken, and outputs at the footage's own aspect ratio (45:01).
Time, not money, is the cost

"upwards of 10 minutes for most people"

"it's going to take 20 minutes"
30-second video, mid-build

Her fix
cut 30 seconds to 8
Her first real edit, 11 minutes
"it took several hours"
On stream, the protein video was started around 20:00 and played back finished at 46:01. That is my reading of the timeline, not a figure she gave.
Every price stated, with its date:
30 Mar 2026: "You only pay for your Claude token consumption" (1:00), on a plan of "$20 or $100 per month" (27:00).
3 Jul 2026: "There's no separate credit system you have to pay for" (1:00). She says Sonnet "at medium level thinking" is enough (34:00).
3 Jul 2026: HeyGen's API "starts at $100 per month. I don't know if that's accurate anymore" (59:01).
Voiceover is where money creeps in. Free text to speech is "pretty crappy" (36:01), while HeyGen or ElevenLabs cost money. Skip voiceover.
What needs your yes
Posting any video anywhere. Both videos end in publishing: Remotion's with Blotato scheduling to Instagram (24:01). That is public.
Pasting any API key, such as Blotato's (23:00), HeyGen's or ElevenLabs'.
AI labels. Neither video covers Etsy, TikTok or Instagram rules on AI-made content, and this recipe did not read them. Read each platform's current rule before the first post.
On AI clones she says "I think people should disclose it" (1:00:02).
Any claim on screen. A page count, a price or "printable" wording in a video is a listing claim, and it must match the file.
What to try — one step, tonight
This costs plan tokens only. It needs no API key, stays on your Mac and posts nothing.
Step 5 is the point. The only thing that decides whether this video can ever be used is whether every page in it is a real page.
ALSO MENTIONED
Remotion's other demo types: a data visualization from a public study, and a HeyGen avatar video with added captions and website screenshots (1:00).
Remotion editing real talking-head footage is "still a bit wonky" (16:01). By July her 11-minute YouTube video was edited entirely by Hyperframes (51:30).
She says Remotion templates take "a couple of days of iterating" (13:32). Once you like a style, have Claude "create a skill to remember all the preferences" (55:01).
Turning landscape into 9:16 needs only FFmpeg, not Hyperframes (55:01).
On models: Opus 4.8 on Max, Sonnet 5 on Pro (3:30). The per-scene subagents' model is never shown.
